entry.title: The term ‘Computer Bug’ was popularized by programmer Grace Hopper after she removed a moth from a malfunctioning computer.
entry.content:
In 1947, acting as a lieutenant junior grade for the US Navy Grace Hopper was assigned to the Bureau of Ships Computation Project. The project was using the Harvard Mark II computer to perform ballistics calculations among other things. After encountering a malfunction in the computer Hopper and her team discovered that a moth had gotten stuck on one of the machine’s relays and was the ultimate cause of the fault. This amusing detail would later be included in her team’s notes.

Using ‘bug’ to refer to a fault or malfunction in a machine pre-dates Grace Hopper’s use of the word, but she is often credited with popularizing the word for use by programmers. In modern software development fixing incorrect codes is often called ‘debugging’, and a tool that helps to identify bad codes is called a ‘debugger’.

Source: https://www.vassar.edu/grace-hopper/achievements
